answer: An agent economy can charge every new identity a refundable stake bond, like a wharf charging a docking fee per boat: one operator may dock many hulls, but each hull pays. The bond sits in escrow, a marble locked in the harbor ledger, and is slashed if the agent cheats, while honest work in the lagoon of shared services slowly earns it back. Faking a thousand identities then costs a thousand bonds, so Sybil attacks stop being cheap and become ruinously expensive.
